html:
Kaarta was a kingdom of the Bambara people in what is now western Mali, ruled by the Massassi dynasty. The map shows it from 1783 to 1815.

It arose in the century after the fall of the Songhai Empire, when Bambara warrior groups formed new states along the upper Niger. The Massassi were related to the rulers of Ségou, the other Bambara kingdom, and the two were bitter rivals. Kaarta's centre moved north-west over time, and from the late 1700s its capital was at Nioro.

Like Ségou, Kaarta was a non-Muslim warrior state that lived by farming, tribute and raiding. In 1854 and 1855 the Muslim reformer Umar Tall conquered it, the first step in building his Toucouleur Empire.
